title: VPC adoption paths & stakeholder playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a pragmatic, stakeholder-focused guide to surface the decision drivers that accelerate VPC/private (control plane in customer network) adoption for regulated workloads. It is meant for SDRs, AE pre-sales, solutions engineers, and product marketing to use as a single-sheet reference during discovery and negotiation.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: customers who say they need ‘private’ for regulation, security, or data residency.
- Not a technical runbook; this is sales-facing messaging + objection handling mapped to technical responses.
- Prioritizes speed to proof-of-value + minimizing legal/timing drag.

High-level adoption paths (quick summary):
1) Fastproof (3–6 weeks): Hosted control plane but with dedicated tenancy and strict contract clauses + customer-managed KMS. Use for early POC where latency and model iteration matter and legal can accept contract controls.
2) VPC-control-plane (6–12 weeks): Redwood control plane lives in customer VPC (managed by Redwood account) or private control plane with network peering. Best when compliance requires private management and auditability.
3) On-prem bundle (12–20 weeks): Full private deployment package including on-prem inference nodes, local control plane instance, and optional air-gapped delivery. Reserved for highest-regulated industries or data residency laws.

Stakeholder cheat-sheets (use these as one-liners + short scripts)

CISO / Head of Security
- Key concerns: data egress, auditability, key management, vulnerability patching, breach liability.
- One-line positioning: “We support a VPC-hosted control plane with customer KMS and full audit logs — so telemetry and config never leave your network unless you opt-in.”
- Technical bridge language: encrypted control plane endpoints, customer-managed KMS (HSM optional), per-token and request-level audit events, allowlist of egress IPs, mTLS to Redwood agents.
- Objection script: ‘Who is responsible for patching?’ -> ‘‘Redwood provides a managed control plane package where we push security updates but with a maintenance window you control; for fully on-prem we ship update artifacts and a secure update channel.’’
- Ask: provide network diagram and list of required legal guards; schedule SRE/infra deep-dive.

Platform/Infrastructure Lead
- Key concerns: latency, throughput isolation, scaling, observability into inference performance.
- One-line positioning: “We offer both reserved pools and private nodes with deterministic throughput guarantees and per-route SLOs so you can map traffic to capacity tiers.”
- Technical bridge language: autoscaling policy examples, QoS controls, token-level latency histograms, traces to model shard and kernel performance.
- Objection script: ‘We can just run open-source on our GPUs’ -> ‘Yes, but our runtime includes kernel selection and batching optimizations that reduce token cost and simplify lifecycle upgrades — we provide rollouts and fallbacks to reduce operational risk.’
- Ask: baseline perf test with two representative prompts and request sample load profile.

Compliance / Legal / Audit
- Key concerns: records retention, data segmentation, right-to-audit, subprocessor lists.
- One-line positioning: “Control plane in your VPC + configurable retention and exportable audit bundles make compliance evidence straightforward.”
- Technical bridge language: immutable audit archives, exportable CSV/JSON logs, optional SIEM integration, signed attestations for retention windows.
- Objection script: ‘We need proof we won’t be subpoenaed to disclose customer data’ -> ‘Control plane logs and data stay in your environment; Redwood’s hosted telemetry excludes payloads unless explicitly opted in.’
- Ask: define retention SLAs and export cadence; assign legal point of contact.

Procurement / Finance
- Key concerns: TCO, baseline vs burst pricing, exit costs.
- One-line positioning: “Reserved private capacity lowers per-token cost while predictable contracts reduce surprise spend.”
- Technical bridge language: cost model with reserved baseline + burst credit, migration playbook, data-evacuation checklist.
- Objection script: ‘We worry about vendor lock-in’ -> ‘We provide model artifacts and exportable configs; fallback modes let you run in a self-managed runtime if you choose to leave.’
- Ask: request cost model template and example 12-month TCO with current query profile.

Competitive framing (short):
- Public LLM API providers (e.g., cloud-LLM): Strength = fastest to start; Weakness = limited control for regulated data and weaker audit bundles. Response: emphasize private control-plane option and explicit data handling contract.
- Self-hosted runtime vendors: Strength = full control; Weakness = long ops ramp and missing managed rollouts/observability. Response: position Redwood as hybrid — managed controls plus exports and upgrade artifacts.
- Managed infra + marketplace vendors: Strength = infrastructure familiarity; Weakness = less model/serving optimizations. Response: highlight performance wins from serving runtime (batching/KV cache) that reduce run costs and simplify QoS.

Common buyer objections + short rebuttals (battle-ready)
- Objection: ‘We can’t have an external control plane.’
  Rebuttal: ‘We offer options: control plane in your VPC (managed by Redwood), or a customer-hosted control plane with Redwood agents. Both provide the same API and rollout semantics.’
- Objection: ‘Who owns the keys and telemetry?’
  Rebuttal: ‘Customer always controls encryption keys in VPC option; telemetry is configurable and payloads can be redacted at the edge.’
- Objection: ‘Performance will suffer vs hosted.’
  Rebuttal: ‘We’ve benchmarked typical enterprise prompts on private nodes and achieve parity via optimized kernels and batching; we publish sample runbooks to size capacity.’
- Objection: ‘This will add months to launch.’
  Rebuttal: ‘Start with a fastproof: hosted with contract controls and KMS while parallelizing network and legal approvals for VPC/on-prem path.’

Suggested proof-of-value (POV) plan (3-step)
1) Discovery week: collect compliance checklist, traffic profile, and 2–3 representative prompts.
2) Fastproof (2–6 weeks): hosted-dedicated or VPC-hosted control plane trial. Focus on functional acceptance, latency checks, and audit logs sample.
3) Harden & migrate (4–10 weeks): CNI/peering setup, KMS integration, runbook handover, and enterprise training.

Demo / scoping agenda (30–60 min)
- 0–5m: Introductions, objective & constraints (legal/regulatory must-haves).
- 5–15m: High-level architecture: control plane options, where logs & keys live.
- 15–30m: Show a short perf demo (example prompt) + autoscaling behavior.
- 30–45m: Walk through audit export + retention UI + SIEM export mock.
- 45–60m: Next steps, timelines, and decision checkpoints.

Artifacts to attach to sales packet (recommended)
- Architecture diagram variants (hosted-control-plane, vpc-control-plane, on-prem).
- Short TCO template (12-month) with reserved/burst lines.
- Audit sample bundle (redacted).
- SRE/ops runbook excerpt for patching and incident handling.
- Regulatory checklist mapping to built features (e.g., HIPAA, SOC2, GDPR).

Decision matrix (one-sentence guidance)
- If regulation mandates data never leave customer network -> On-prem bundle.
- If auditability + KMS control suffice -> VPC control plane.
- If speed to market is primary and legal can accept strong contract controls -> Fastproof (hosted with contract).

Next steps (actionable)
- For AE: send POV checklist + TCO template within 24 hours of discovery.
- For Solutions Engineer: schedule infra deep-dive within 3 business days.
- For PM/Prod-Marketing: iterate collateral list above into a one-pager per stakeholder.

Open questions / to validate with product/infra teams:
- SLA language for VPC-hosted control plane (uptime, maintenance windows).
- Default telemetry retention periods and tooling to export immutable archives.
- Patch cadence and secure update mechanism for on-prem control planes.

Notes and conversation fragments (scratchpad):
- Prospect X: legal will only sign if keys are customer-owned — map to VPC + KMS integration play.
- Prospect Y: wants 'air-gapped' for specific model training — needs on-prem and devops bundle.
- Internal ask: create 1 pager comparing attack surface: hosted vs vpc vs on-prem.

Owner notes: pull-in infra for two-week readiness checklist and prioritize shipping an audit sample archive for sales.

End of playbook.
